name: @plexui/ui
description: The most flexible UI kit for React. Production-grade components with pixel-perfect Figma parity.

setup.provider: Wrap your app with <PlexUIProvider linkComponent={Link}> from "@plexui/ui/components/PlexUIProvider" (your router's Link, or "a")

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Vertically stacked panels that expand to reveal content, with one or several items open at a time and full keyboard navigation.

props.name: type
props.description: Whether one item or many can be open at a time

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when the open item(s) change

props.name: collapsible
props.description: When type="single", allow closing the open item

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="shipping">
<Accordion.Item value="shipping">
  <Accordion.Trigger>What are your shipping options?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>
    We offer standard (5–7 business days), express (2–3 days), and overnight shipping…
  </Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="returns">
  <Accordion.Trigger>What is your return policy?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="support">
  <Accordion.Trigger>How can I contact customer support?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>Reach us by email, live chat, or phone Monday–Friday…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>

examples.name: Single
examples.code:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="trial">
{items.map((item) => (
  <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
    <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
))}
</Accordion>
examples.details: Default shape. type="single" + collapsible lets users close the currently open item; without collapsible, one item is always open.

examples.name: Multiple
examples.code:
<Accordion type="multiple" defaultValue={["notifications"]}>
{items.map((item) => (
  <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
    <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
))}
</Accordion>
examples.details: Use type="multiple" when readers can keep several sections open at once: settings pages, long FAQs, step-by-step references.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.code:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible>
<Accordion.Item value="history">
  <Accordion.Trigger>Can I see my usage history?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="audit" disabled>
  <Accordion.Trigger>Audit log export (Enterprise only)</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
<Accordion.Item value="two-factor">
  <Accordion.Trigger>How do I enable two-factor auth?</Accordion.Trigger>
  <Accordion.Content>…</Accordion.Content>
</Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>
examples.details: Pass disabled to an Accordion.Item to make it read-only. The row stays visible so the reader understands the section exists; keyboard focus skips it.

examples.name: Card
examples.code:
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Subscription & billing</Card.Title>
  <Card.Description>Common questions about plans, invoices, and cancellations.</Card.Description>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="plans">
    {items.map((item) => (
      <Accordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value}>
        <Accordion.Trigger>{item.trigger}</Accordion.Trigger>
        <Accordion.Content>{item.content}</Accordion.Content>
      </Accordion.Item>
    ))}
  </Accordion>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
examples.details: Composed inside Card, the most common landing-page FAQ pattern.

components.name: Alert
components.description: Inline message for notices and warnings with semantic colors, variants, a title, a description, action slots, and a dismiss control.

props.name: indicator
props.description: Custom indicator or false to hide

props.name: banner
props.description: Full-width strip: square corners, lines above and below only

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Alert
title="Scheduled maintenance"
description="We'll be offline 2 - 4 AM UTC on July 14 while we upgrade our database."
actions={<Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Dismiss</Button>}
/>

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code:
<Alert
color="primary"
variant="outline"
title="Scheduled maintenance on Saturday, 2-4 AM PT"
description={<>Track status updates on <TextLink color="currentcolor" href="#">status page</TextLink></>}
/>
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the alert using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Title
examples.code: <Alert title="Your current access level limits what you can view or modify" />
examples.details: You can optionally include a title for your alert with the title prop.

examples.name: Description
examples.code:
<Alert
description={
  <>
    We're working on centralizing SCIM and invite settings. For now, setup is handled within individual product settings. <TextLink href="#">Learn more</TextLink>
  </>
}
/>
examples.details: You can optionally include description text for your alert with the description prop.

examples.name: Actions
examples.code:
<Alert
variant="soft"
color="warning"
title="Password expires in 3 days"
description="Update it now to avoid losing access to your account."
actions={<Button color="primary" pill>Update password</Button>}
/>
examples.details: You can add actions to the alert with the actions prop, which accepts ReactNode. Combine with onDismiss to add a dismiss button.

examples.name: Action placement
examples.code:
<Alert
title="Our terms of service has been updated"
description="We've updated our terms to clarify how we handle data, billing, and user permissions. Please review and accept the latest terms to avoid impacting your service."
actions={(
  <>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Set reminder</Button>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>Review terms</Button>
  </>
)}
actionsPlacement="bottom"
/>
examples.details: Actions are automatically positioned in the alert by default. You can force a specific position with the actionsPlacement prop by passing either 'end' or 'bottom'.

examples.name: Indicator
examples.code:
<Alert
indicator={<Lightbulb />}
description={
  <>
    We're working on centralizing SCIM and invite settings. For now, setup is handled within individual product settings. <TextLink href="#">Learn more</TextLink>
  </>
}
/>
examples.details: Alert provides an indicator icon by default. You can override it by passing a custom icon to indicator, or pass indicator={'{false}'} to hide it entirely.

examples.name: Dismissible
examples.code:
<Alert
className="items-start"
title="Try our new dashboard layout"
description="We've introduced a streamlined layout that makes using the dashboard even easier. You can switch back any time."
actions={(
  <>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Dismiss</Button>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>Try it</Button>
  </>
)}
/>
examples.details: The suggested approach for dismissible notices is to use labeled buttons via actions. You can also provide onDismiss to render a dismiss button in the alert chrome.

examples.name: Banner
examples.code:
<Alert
banner
color="caution"
variant="soft"
indicator={false}
description="You are offline. Changes will sync when the connection is back."
/>
examples.details: Use banner for a full-width strip across the top or bottom of a page or panel: offline, read-only, a new version. It drops the rounded corners and keeps only the lines above and below. Pass indicator={'{false}'} for a plain strip.

<Avatar name="Jane" color="discovery" />

components.name: Avatar
components.description: An avatar for user identities that shows an initial, a photo or an icon, with overflow counts, semantic colors and roundness options.

props.name: name
props.description: Display name; used for text initial when no image/icon

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: A variety of avatar types: text, image, icon, and overflow.

examples.name: Text
examples.code: <Avatar name="David" size={48} />
examples.details: For text-based avatars, a single initial is displayed based on the name prop passed to the component.

examples.name: Image
examples.code:
<Avatar
name="Tyler"
imageUrl="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552"
size={48}
/>
examples.details: To display an image avatar, provide an absolute URL to the image with imageUrl. Images will have a soft fade entrance once loaded, or fallback to a text display if the image fail to load.

examples.name: Icon
examples.code:
<Avatar
Icon={Robot}
size={48}
/>
examples.details: To display an icon avatar, provide an icon to render to the Icon prop. The name prop is not used in this case, and can be omitted.

examples.name: Overflow count
examples.code: <Avatar overflowCount={9} size={48} />
examples.details: To display an overflow avatar, provide a number to the overflowCount prop. The number will be automatically formatted and scaled to fit.

examples.name: Sizing
examples.code: <Avatar name="David" size={48} />
examples.details: To size the avatar, pass a number to the size property, which will set the width and height in pixels. Text and icon avatars will scale their sizes dynamically based on this value.

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the avatar using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Roundness
examples.code: <Avatar name="Acme, co." color="primary" variant="solid" size={48} className="rounded-lg" />
examples.details: By default, avatars are fully rounded. You can override this by passing a Tailwind rounding class to className.

name="Will"
size={48}
onClick={saySup}
/>
examples.details: Avatars can be used as interactive elements by passing an onClick handler. The avatar will automatically apply semantic and visual interaction styles.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description: The trail of pages that leads to the current one, above a page title, with links, plain steps and the current page.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: sm above a compact header, md above a page title

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/">Home</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/settings">Settings</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Members</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: Breadcrumb renders a nav landmark named "Breadcrumb" around an ordered list. An item with href is a link (internal paths use the linkComponent of PlexUIProvider, such as your router's link); the current item is plain text marked aria-current="page".

examples.name: Sizes
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb size="sm">
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/projects">Projects</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/projects/website">Website</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Deployments</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: Use size="sm" for a trail above a compact header; the default md sits above a page title.

examples.name: Separator
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb separator="/">
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/acme">acme</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/acme/design-system">design-system</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>README.md</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: A small chevron stands between items by default. Pass any node to separator, such as a slash for file paths. Separators are hidden from assistive technology.

examples.name: Long trails
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/">Workspace</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/accounts">Customer accounts</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item href="/accounts/northwind">Northwind Traders</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item>Archived</Breadcrumb.Item>
<Breadcrumb.Item current>Invoice 2024-0193</Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: A trail that does not fit wraps onto the next line instead of leaving the screen. An item without href is a plain step; give it onClick to make it act as a button.

props.name: href
props.description: Link destination. Internal paths use the linkComponent of PlexUIProvider

props.name: to
props.description: Router destination, for link components that take to

props.name: current
props.description: The current page: plain text marked aria-current="page"

props.name: onClick

components.name: Button Group
components.description: Join buttons into a single visual unit for toolbars, steppers, split buttons and search affordances.

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup><Button uniform aria-label="Go back"><ArrowLeftSm /></Button></ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button>Pin</Button>
  <Button>Tag</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button>Bookmark</Button>
  <Button uniform aria-label="More options"><DotsHorizontal /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>

examples.name: Orientation
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom controls">
<Button uniform aria-label="Zoom in"><PlusSm /></Button>
<Button uniform aria-label="Zoom out"><Minus /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Pass orientation="vertical" to stack the buttons, which is useful for + / − steppers, zoom controls, or any vertical toolbar.

examples.name: Size
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button size="sm">Small</Button>
<Button size="sm">Button</Button>
<Button size="sm">Group</Button>
<Button size="sm" uniform aria-label="Add"><PlusSm /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Set size on every Button inside the group so corner radii match. Mix icon-only (uniform) with text buttons. Each child keeps its own padding.

examples.name: Nested
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Pager">
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button size="sm">1</Button>
  <Button size="sm">2</Button>
  <Button size="sm">3</Button>
  <Button size="sm">4</Button>
  <Button size="sm">5</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button size="sm" uniform aria-label="Previous page"><ArrowLeftSm /></Button>
  <Button size="sm" uniform aria-label="Next page"><ArrowRightSm /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Place ButtonGroup inside ButtonGroup to create visually separated sub-groups. The outer group automatically adds a small gap between children; pagination + arrow nav is the canonical pattern.

examples.name: Separator
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm"><Undo /> Undo</Button>
<ButtonGroup.Separator />
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" size="sm">Redo <Redo /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Drop a ButtonGroup.Separator between items to add a visible divider, commonly used for Undo / Redo pairs or any "two related actions" toolbar.

examples.name: Split
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary"><Filter /> Filter</Button>
<ButtonGroup.Separator />
<Button variant="soft" color="secondary" uniform aria-label="Add filter">
  <Plus />
</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: The classic split button: an action joined to a secondary affordance via ButtonGroup.Separator. Useful for Save / Save-As, Filter / Add-filter, Delete / Undo.

examples.name: Input
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Input placeholder="Search docs..." />
<Button aria-label="Search"><SearchSm /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Join an Input to a trailing Button for inline search, token entry, or URL shorteners. The input flexes to fill the row; the button hugs its content.

examples.name: Input group
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button pill uniform aria-label="Add attachment"><Plus /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Input
    pill
    placeholder={voiceEnabled ? "Recording your idea…" : "Describe a component…"}
    disabled={voiceEnabled}
    endAdornment={
      <Input.AdornmentButton
        color={voiceEnabled ? "caution" : undefined}
        aria-label="Toggle voice mode"
        aria-pressed={voiceEnabled}
        onClick={() => setVoiceEnabled((prev) => !prev)}
      >
        <Mic />
      </Input.AdornmentButton>
    }
  />
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Richer composition for message composers: wrap each slot (leading action, flexible Input) in its own ButtonGroup so the outer group inserts a gap between them. The voice toggle rides inside the input via endAdornment. Use Input.AdornmentButton: it sizes off the input's own size token so the button stays concentric with the pill at every size.

examples.name: Dropdown menu
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button>Export</Button>
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <Button uniform aria-label="More export options"><ChevronDownMd /></Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content align="end">
    <Menu.Item><FileImage /> PNG image</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item><FileCode /> SVG vector</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item><FileDocument /> PDF document</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Item><Copy /> Copy as code</Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Item><Link /> Copy share link</Menu.Item>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Compose a primary action with a Menu trigger for follow-up options. Common for Export / Format, Save / Save-As, Share / ….

examples.name: Select
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Select options={units} value={unit} onChange={(o) => setUnit(o.value)} variant="outline" pill={false} block={false} />
  <Input placeholder="2.50" inputMode="decimal" />
</ButtonGroup>
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button uniform aria-label="Log weight"><ArrowRight /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Mix a Select and an Input inside one ButtonGroup for unit pickers, currency entry, or any "qualifier + value" pattern. Wrap each slot in a nested ButtonGroup to get a gap between the compound field and the send affordance.

examples.name: Popover
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
<Button><Sparkles /> Generate</Button>
<Popover>
  <Popover.Trigger>
    <Button uniform aria-label="More generate options"><ChevronDownMd /></Button>
  </Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content side="bottom" align="end" className="p-4">
    <Card variant="ghost" size="sm">
      <Card.Header>
        <Card.Title>Generate a component</Card.Title>
        <Card.Description>Describe what to build in plain English.</Card.Description>
      </Card.Header>
      <Card.Content>
        <Textarea placeholder="A login form with email and password…" rows={3} />
      </Card.Content>
      <Card.Footer>
        <Card.Description>Plex will draft the code and preview it live.</Card.Description>
      </Card.Footer>
    </Card>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Same split-button shape, but the trailing trigger opens a Popover instead of a menu, useful for richer panels (prompt composers, notification preferences, link previews).

components.name: Button
components.description: Button with four variants (solid, soft, outline, ghost), eight semantic colors, icon slots, loading, and block layout.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height and default gutter/icon size

props.name: gutterSize
props.description: Horizontal padding size; defaults from size

props.name: iconSize
props.description: Size of icons in children; defaults from size

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: A showcase of Button's key styles: solid, soft, outline, ghost, and icon-only.

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code: ( )} />
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the button using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Sizing & roundness
examples.details: Control height with size and horizontal padding with gutterSize. Use pill for fully rounded corners. size sets the button to a specific control height, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding. Each size provides default values for gutterSize and iconSize props, as well as font-size. Each of these values can be overridden independently. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied to the button.

examples.name: Icons
examples.code:
<Button color="secondary" size="lg" uniform variant="ghost" aria-label="Add">
<PlusLg />
</Button>
examples.details: Add icons as children. Sizing is automatic via the iconSize prop. Default values for iconSize are provided through the size prop, but you can pass the prop directly to change the defaults. For icon-only buttons, there are two common approaches: Square: create perfect square icon buttons with the uniform prop. When uniform is passed, gutterSize is ignored. Combine with pill to make circular icons. Tighter gutters: applying a smaller gutterSize than size can create well-sized, but not exactly square, icon buttons.

examples.name: Block
examples.details: Create full-width buttons with the block prop.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.code: <Button disabled>Submit</Button>
examples.details: Use disabled to both visually and accessibly disable a button.

examples.name: Inert
examples.code: <Button inert>Submit</Button>
examples.details: Use inert to accessibly disable a button without any visual changes. Note: For accessibility reasons, disabled is used instead of applying inert directly to the button. Visual disablement in the disabled prop is applied via [data-disable].

examples.name: Loading
examples.code: <Button loading size="xl" pill><ArrowUp /> Click to load</Button>
examples.details: Use loading to display a loading indicator in the button, fading out the current content. Interactions will be prevented by default during this state, by providing a default value for inert to true. You can override this behavior directly with inert, or use disabled to add visual disablement.

examples.name: Selected
examples.code:
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger>
  <Button selected variant="solid">Click to open</Button>
</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content minWidth="auto" className="p-4 text-sm">
  <ShimmerText className="font-medium text-secondary">Button should look selected</ShimmerText>
</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
